headline: Local Father Implements 'Parental Supervision' By Physically Standing Behind Teenager's Shoulder During Entire Scroll Through Instagram
body:
Following recent judicial suggestions regarding digital safety, 47-year-old software architect Rajesh Sharma has successfully inaugurated an ‘Analog Child Mode’ for his 16-year-old son’s social media usage by simply standing directly behind him in the living room for the duration of every scrolling session. The initiative, which requires no software updates or complex privacy settings, ensures that the teenager’s consumption of content is mediated by the heavy, rhythmic breathing of a parent standing exactly six inches from his left ear.

“The court talked about digital safety, but I believe in tactile intervention,” said Sharma, who occasionally taps his son on the shoulder to ask, ‘Is this reel contributing to your JEE preparation?’ whenever the algorithm serves a video of a dog dancing to a trending pop song. “There is no need for a ‘child mode’ toggle when you have a father who has mastered the art of looming. Every time he tries to click on a meme, I just clear my throat, and he immediately switches to a documentary about tectonic plates.”

Experts note that while the teenager’s ‘screen time’ has plummeted by 90 percent, his heart rate during leisure activities has reached a consistent athletic peak. Neighbors report that the ‘supervision’ is so thorough that even the teenager’s attempts to open a private browser tab are met with a swift, preemptive lecture on the history of the Indian Railways. Sharma maintains that until the digital infrastructure catches up with his parenting, he will remain the most effective ‘content filter’ in the house.
caption: Forget software updates, the most effective child mode is just your dad standing behind you for three hours. Modern problems require 1990s solutions. #DigitalSafety #ParentingHacks #TechNews (satire)
igHook: Tag a friend who would be terrified if their parents actually tried this.

sourceHeadline.title: 'Internet access is fundamental right': SC suggests ‘child mode’ for social media accounts

judgeVerdict.reasoning: Candidate 1 stands out for its vivid, visceral imagery—the 'heavy, rhythmic breathing' of a parent looming is a genuinely funny, specific detail that elevates the premise. It manages the deadpan tone well without relying on 'formulaic quote scaffolding' or over-explaining the joke, and it feels like a relatable, warm observation of parenting dynamics rather than just another cynical take on digital regulation.

safetyVerdict.reasoning: The article uses a fictional, archetypal persona 'Rajesh Sharma' to satirize parental overreach in the digital age. The content is harmless, whimsical, and focuses on universal relatable parenting tropes without targeting real individuals, religious, caste, or ethnic groups.
